messages:
alex: Observed repeated inference p99 spikes in eastus around 15:10 UTC, correlating with increased tcp retransmits. Noticed packet drops on host e2e-gpu-07. Could be a host-level shaper accidentally applied during a maintenance run.

ops-bot: Alert: inference-slo-eastus p99_latency exceeded threshold (1800ms) for 5m. Metric: tcp_retransmits up 4x.

alex: I pulled `ss -s` on the host, and `ifstat` shows bursty egress stalls. Running `tc -s qdisc` shows a TBF root qdisc with tiny rate. Looks like this config got pushed to a subset of hosts.

alex: Config snippet from host:
```
qdisc tbf 1: root refcnt 2 rate 10Mbit burst 32768b latency 400ms
Sent 12345 bytes  dropped 2390 bytes  overlimits 12 pkts
```

tanya: oof that's too low for intra-cluster RPC. Our kernels coalesce large RDMA-like flows into TCP frames; TBF + small burst will cause packet queuing and retransmits. Can you `tc -s filter show dev eth0`?

prateek: Adding that — filters show a `fwmark`-based filter intended for batch backups but matched `gpu-*` hosts due to a regex bug in the shipper.

prateek: Filter output:
```
filter protocol ip pref 1 u32
filter match 0/0 at 12
action ok
```

kim: So basically a backup shaping rule was applied onto inference hosts. That will increase latency non-linearly for short-tail requests (small token counts) since packets get queued. Also increases p99 because retransmits re-order and extend kernel timers.

alex: I rolled the local change removing TBF on the affected host: `tc qdisc del dev eth0 root`. p99 dropped back toward baseline within ~30s.

tanya: Nice. Can we confirm scope of rollout? Which hosts had the bad filter?

prateek: Querying fleet: the shipper CL id 6021 had pattern `gpu-.*-backup` but we accidentally globbed `gpu-.*` in the agent. Matches: e2e-gpu-05, -06, -07, -09. Only eastus pool.

kim: Action items: short-term revert shipper CL 6021, roll a fix to the glob, add explicit allowed-list for backup shapers. Also add a canary guard so qdisc changes only apply to hosts with label `backup: true`.

alex: Also: add a health-check rule in the deploy pipeline that rejects `tc` changes unless `tcp_retransmits` stays within 2x baseline on a 2-host canary for 5m.

ops-bot: Note created: INCIDENT-2028. Assigning to eng-infra.

prateek: I'll open a fix PR and a rollback playbook. Will include a one-liner to check `tc -s qdisc` across fleet and compare `dropped` counters.

kim: FYI, we saw a similar pattern a while back caused by MTU mismatch + shaper. Put a short test in the infra QA: simulate small MTU and shaper to reproduce regression.

alex: TL;DR: misapplied TBF/shaper from backup shipper to inference hosts caused packet drops and inference p99 regression in eastus. Reverted on affected hosts; rolling fleet-wide guard + deploy-checks.

tanya: +1. Please paste PR link when ready. :thumbsup:

prateek: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/489 (draft) — includes fix + guard + playbook.

kim: After PR merges, let's schedule a small controlled run during low traffic window to validate.

alex: I'll keep monitoring metrics and post updates. Thanks all. :face_with_monocle:
